editorial:
Imagine getting ripped off by a sleazy used-car salesman who then pretends you don't even exist. That is exactly what happens to Gösta, a simple hairdresser who just wanted a decent ride. You will love the dynamic when his brother Rolle gets out of prison and decides to help him get even. Instead of just fighting, they decide to play a game of high-stakes greed. They start a fake investment company called Parabola to trick the salesman and his shady friends into handing over their cash. It is a classic underdog story with a funny, rebellious vibe that makes you root for the scammers because the victims are even worse people.

The movie keeps a great pace, and the acting makes the dialogue feel real and punchy. You will find the way the scam snowballs out of control both stressful and hilarious. While some of the 80s style feels a bit dated, the humor still hits home today. If you enjoy stories about clever cons, you should definitely track this one down.
endingExplained: The scam eventually grows too big for Gösta and Rolle to handle as more criminals invest their money. In the final act, the tension peaks when the investors demand their money back. However, the brothers manage to outsmart the greedy businessmen one last time. They walk away with a decent amount of cash while the crooked dealers are left with nothing, proving that the biggest fools are the ones who think they can cheat everyone else.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves clever con-artist stories and underdog victories.
